what: The scorer on small streams of score records: crossings, events with their captured frames, and the histogram. Every expected value was worked BY HAND from the definition in model/scorer.py's docstring; the working is in each case's 'worked' lines. The score records are written here by hand too: the scorer is fed them directly, so nothing here depends on the detector core.
definition: A record with the settling flag (flags bit 0) is left out of every count. A counted record is above when score > threshold, strictly. An event is captured at each counted record that is above and whose predecessor was not above or not counted. Its pre is min(configured pre, index); its post is the configured post, or fewer if the stream ends. The histogram has hist_bins bins of width 2^hist_shift from hist_lo; a score under hist_lo counts in below, one past the last bin in above.
format: frames gives, for each profile, frame i for i = 0..; in s24x3 the three channels differ. events[n].frames lists the INDEXES of the frames captured, oldest first. overflow_at is the index of the first record carrying the overflow flag (flags bit 1, value 2), or null. completed_after[i] is the number of events that are complete once record i has been fed and before the next is; completed_at_close is the number once the stream is closed.

cases.name: crossings-events-histogram
cases.why: Index 1 scores exactly the threshold and is NOT above. Index 2 is one above it. Index 6 is a settling record with a large score, left out. Indexes 3, 5 and 9 land in the last bin, index 7 beyond it, index 4 below the first.
worked: counted: every record but index 6, so 9; excluded: 1
above (score > 10): index 2 (11), 3 (12), 5 (15), 7 (16), 9 (14): 5 crossings. Index 1 scores 10, which is not greater than 10
events: index 2 (index 1 was not above); not index 3 (index 2 was above); index 5 (index 4 was not); index 7 (index 6 was not counted); index 9 (index 8 was not)
event at 2: pre 2 (frames 0, 1), post 1 (frame 3). At 5: frames 3, 4 | 5 | 6. At 7: frames 5, 6 | 7 | 8. At 9: frames 7, 8 | 9, and the stream ends, so post 0
bins of width 4 from 0: bin 0 holds 0..3, bin 1 holds 4..7, bin 2 holds 8..11, bin 3 holds 12..15
bins 1, 1, 2, 3; below 1; above 1; and 1 + 1 + 2 + 3 + 1 + 1 = 9, the counted records
the overflow flag is first seen at index 8
complete: the event at 2 once frame 3 is fed; the event at 5 once frame 6 is; the event at 7 once frame 8 is; the event at 9 only at close. So 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3 and then 4

cases.name: the-streams-ends-cut-the-windows
cases.why: The first record is above, so its event has no frame before it. The second event is two frames from the start and one from the end, with a configured window of 3 before and 2 after. A negative hist_lo, bins of width 1.
worked: above (score > 0): index 0 (1) and index 2 (5): 2 crossings; index 1 scores 0, not above
event at 0: no predecessor; pre min(3, 0) = 0; post 2 (frames 1, 2)
event at 2: index 1 was not above; pre min(3, 2) = 2 (frames 0, 1); one frame is left, so post 1 (frame 3)
bins of width 1 from -2: bin 0 holds -2, bin 1 holds -1, bin 2 holds 0
1 -> above;  0 -> bin 2;  5 -> above;  -2 -> bin 0
bins 1, 0, 1; below 0; above 2; 4 counted
complete: the event at 0 once frame 2 is fed; the event at 2 only at close. So 0, 0, 1, 1 and then 2

cases.name: a-post-of-zero
cases.why: With no frame wanted after the crossing, an event is complete the moment its own record is fed: its captured frames end with the crossing's frame, its post is 0, and it is in the list before the next record arrives. A scorer that held it open would add later frames to it, or deliver it late.
worked: above (score > 3): index 0 (4), 1 (5), 3 (9), 5 (7): 4 crossings
events: index 0 (no predecessor); not index 1 (index 0 was above); index 3 (index 2 was not); index 5 (index 4 was not)
event at 0: pre min(1, 0) = 0, post 0: frame 0 alone. At 3: frame 2 | 3. At 5: frame 4 | 5
complete at once, each on its own record: 1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3 and then 3 at close
bins of width 2 from 0: bin 0 holds 0..1, bin 1 holds 2..3, bin 2 holds 4..5, bin 3 holds 6..7
4 -> bin 2;  5 -> bin 2;  2 -> bin 1;  9 -> above;  1 -> bin 0;  7 -> bin 3
bins 1, 1, 2, 1; below 0; above 1; 6 counted
